rules.covers: AI call inside a loop cost $900
background task retrying forever (proxy: any outbound request inside a while loop)
every table that stores customer emails is tracked (tagged)
who changed what: objects reaching tagged tables call the audit function unconditionally

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Cap on AI spend (a budget or dollar limit)
Background task retries forever: whether a retry loop has an attempt cap or backoff
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how; statement.containment only forbids outbound requests inside a while loop, so bounded retries are also flagged and retries via a task schedule are not seen

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Audit records what changed (the changes payload), not just that the audit function is called

ask_parts_not_covered.why: needs runtime/org process: tags decide which policies apply, and the workspace must not be changed

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Who changed what in a write done outside the audit call (e.g. direct db.direct_query)

assumptions: customer emails = email-typed fields named email or requester_email: customers.email, users.email, newsletter_subscribers.email, patients.email, support_tickets.requester_email
tenants.billing_email is text, not email type, so it is excluded by field_types
record_audit_event is the audit function (it writes audit_log)
ai.agent.run is the AI call statement name, as used in nightly_ticket_summaries
while/for/foreach are valid must_not_be_inside block names (taken from the stack.size_limit description, not from a param enum)
the customer wants advisory policies; I did not choose blocking
confusions: No check covers cost, spend or loop-bound logic; the catalogue has no loop or retry check, so the cost half of the ask rests on a containment proxy with no guidance from the skill

The skill lists which block names must_not_be_inside accepts only indirectly (try_catch examples and the stack.size_limit description); no enum or list of block names is given, so I guessed foreach, for and while
Template CONF-010's title says logged-in endpoints only, but I used it for audit; the template gives no guidance for adding a function param, so I had to decide that myself
Template CONF-012 has no field_types example and its fill example uses text fields; the email-typed choice was my call
The skill says tags decide which policies apply but does not say how a tag gets onto a table in the first place; it only says propose it for the user
object.tagged_table_access forces login on every endpoint reaching a tagged table, which the template title doesn't reflect; the skill should say so for this template
xano policy parse plain output omits severity when it is medium (the -o json output and the file itself keep it); this looked like a dropped field until I checked
wished_for: A cost/loop check, or at least a recipe for bounding AI and retry loops (e.g. max iterations on while, a call-count cap)
A list of valid block names for must_be_inside / must_not_be_inside
A template for audit trails that also checks the changes payload
Guidance on how to tag tables safely (who proposes, how the tag is applied) for the pii case
parse_errors_seen: Rule warning: CONF-010.R1: table_tags "pii" is on no table in this workspace, so no access to it is judged (expected: the tag is not yet applied)
why_confidence: The policies parse and map to real names, and two cost patterns and the tagging/audit half have checks. But the spend cap and bounded-retry parts aren't checkable; the loop rules are proxies; and I haven't run evaluate, so the predicted findings are unverified.
